metaDescription: Six five-blade herb scissors compared on cleaning combs, covers, rivets, length and dishwasher listings, from Cuisinart and X-Chef to JOFUYU and POROMI.
introParagraphs: Herb scissors with multiple parallel blades solve a small but annoying kitchen problem. Chopping parsley, chives or cilantro with a knife is slow, bruises the leaves and leaves green stains on the board, while a single-blade scissor leaves you snipping one cut at a time. A five-blade pair makes several cuts at once, so a few squeezes turn a bunch of herbs into evenly sized pieces right over the dish.

We evaluated six distinct pairs for this guide, from the 8.5 inch Cuisinart herb shears to the compact 7.5 inch Jenaluca, with the JOFUYU, POROMI, SASACIA and X-Chef in between. Many listings look almost identical, so we focused on the details that actually differ: overall length, how the blades are fixed, whether a cleaning comb and a cover are included, what the handles are made of and what each listing says about dishwasher cleaning. The comparison is based on product specs and buyer feedback, not on a lab bench.

The real test of any multi-blade herb scissor is cleaning. Herbs pack into the gaps between blades, so a pair that comes with a comb and rinses easily will be used far more often than one that sits in the drawer after one messy attempt. Before you buy, decide how much you value a built-in cleaning kit versus a familiar brand, because that is the main trade between the JOFUYU and the Cuisinart. A pair that is easy to clean will be used often, and a pair that is used often is worth more than a better-sounding listing.

products.name: Cuisinart C77-SHRH Herb Shears
products.description:
The Cuisinart C77-SHRH is an 8.5 inch herb shear with ultra sharp stainless steel blades and soft-grip handles for stability and control. The listing describes five blades on each side that cut herbs and other greens efficiently and precisely.

The longer body gives you more leverage than compact pairs, and the soft-grip handles reduce slipping when your hands are wet. The listing is short, so it does not mention a cover, a cleaning comb or a dishwasher rating. That means you should check the product page for care details before buying.

In practice this is the pair for cooks who value a familiar kitchenware brand and a longer handle. Compared with the 7.5 inch Jenaluca it is bigger and less pocketable, and against the JOFUYU it lacks a stated cleaning kit. It suits cooks who snip herbs often and want a traditional shape.

The JOFUYU herb scissors use five food-grade stainless steel blades firmly locked in place with three solid rivets. The handle interior is TPR rubber for a comfortable non-slip grip.

The cleaning kit is the standout feature. A cleaning brush is included, and the protective cover doubles as a comb that pulls herbs from between the blades. That solves the biggest annoyance of the category, which is stuck herb residue.

The listing does not publish the length or a dishwasher rating in the excerpt we reviewed, so check the product page. Compared with the Cuisinart it adds a brush and a comb cover, and against the POROMI it lists a rivet count. It is a good fit for cooks who want a complete, ready-to-clean package.

The POROMI herb scissors use food-grade stainless steel blades held by reinforced rivets that the maker says keep the blades aligned. A safety cover protects the blades and your hands in storage.

The tradeoff is that the listing gives no length or handle material in the excerpt. Compared with the JOFUYU it states dishwasher safe, and against the X-Chef it is similar in features. It suits cooks who want easy cleaning with a stated machine option.

The X-Chef herb scissors have five sharp blades held together by a heavy-duty steel rivet, with an ergonomic handle for comfortable use. The maker says the five-blade set equals ten knife chops, which captures how it speeds up snipping herbs, basil and chives.

A safety cover and a cleaning comb are included, and the listing says the stainless steel pair is dishwasher safe. The comb helps remove lingering herbs or chives in a few moments. The listing excerpt does not publish the length.

It competes closely with the POROMI on features and stated dishwasher rating. Against the Cuisinart it adds the cover and comb, and compared with the Jenaluca it does not give a compact size. It is a good fit for cooks who want a straightforward kit that cleans easily.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Herbs pack into the gaps between blades, so a cleaning tool matters more here than on any other scissor. The JOFUYU includes a brush and a comb cover, and the POROMI, X-Chef and SASACIA each include a comb. The Cuisinart and Jenaluca excerpts do not mention one. A cover also protects the blades and your fingers in the drawer. Pick a pair with a comb if you hate scrubbing. If you cook with fresh herbs weekly, a brush plus comb kit saves a surprising amount of time, because the comb clears all five gaps in one pass. Rinse before the herb residue dries, since dried leaf is far harder to remove, and always dry the pair fully before you fit the cover.

Five blades must stay aligned or the cut becomes ragged. The JOFUYU uses three rivets, the POROMI uses reinforced rivets and the X-Chef uses a heavy-duty steel rivet. Loose blades are the usual failure on cheap herb scissors. Look for riveted construction and check buyer feedback on alignment. Gently wiggle a pair before you use it, since any play between blades will show up as ragged cuts. If a pair develops looseness, stop using it for food and contact the maker rather than forcing it, because a shifting blade can also nick fingers.

Length changes leverage and storage. The Cuisinart is 8.5 inches while the Jenaluca is 7.5 inches, and the others do not state a length in the excerpt. A longer pair gives more leverage, while a compact pair is easier to control and store. Match it to your hand and drawer. If you are unsure, choose by your drawer first, then by your hand. A tool that fits where you keep it gets used, while an awkward one stays at the back.

A dishwasher claim helps if you hate hand washing. The POROMI, X-Chef and SASACIA state dishwasher safe, while the Cuisinart, JOFUYU and Jenaluca excerpts do not. Heat and detergent can still dull edges over time. A quick hand rinse with a comb is often enough. Treat any dishwasher claim as permission, not a recommendation, and consider hand washing with the comb to protect the edge. Keep the cover off while the blades dry so no moisture sits against the metal.

Herb work involves wet hands, so grip matters. The Cuisinart has soft-grip handles, the JOFUYU has TPR non-slip handles and the Jenaluca fits right and left hands. A secure handle prevents slips. Choose by how your hand feels, if you can try. Wet hands slip on smooth plastic, so a textured or rubbery handle such as the TPR on the JOFUYU gives more confidence. If your hands are small, a lighter body like the Jenaluca is easier to guide.

Multi-blade scissors chop soft herbs and greens well but are not for hard food. The X-Chef claim of five blades equal to ten knife chops describes speed on soft leaves. Woody stems need patience, and paper or crafts can dull blades. Use herb scissors for herbs and keep a separate pair for other tasks. If a recipe needs a rough chop, snip once or twice, and if it needs fine pieces, snip repeatedly across the bunch. The scissors do not replace a knife for dense vegetables, but they beat one for chives and soft leaves.

faq.q: Are multi-blade herb scissors worth it?
faq.a: They are worth it if you cook with fresh herbs often. Five blades make several cuts per squeeze, which saves time compared with a knife. They are less useful for dried herbs or hard food. If you rarely use fresh herbs, a normal scissor is enough. Think about how often you use fresh herbs before deciding how much to spend.

faq.q: How do I clean herb scissors?
faq.a: Rinse them right after use and use the included comb or brush to clear the gaps between blades. The JOFUYU includes both. Dry the blades fully. Herbs that dry on are much harder to remove. Always dry the blades fully after washing and keep the cover off until they are dry.

The POROMI, X-Chef and SASACIA state dishwasher safe in the listings we reviewed. The others do not state it in the excerpts, so check the product page. Heat and detergent can dull blades over time. Check the product page of the exact pair for care instructions before using a machine.

Soft herbs such as basil, parsley, cilantro, chives and green onions work best. Woody stems like rosemary are harder on the blades. The Jenaluca listing mentions tough stems, but go gently. Gather the herbs into a tight bunch and snip across them for the most even pieces.

faq.q: Is a longer or shorter pair better?
faq.a: The Cuisinart at 8.5 inches gives more leverage, and the Jenaluca at 7.5 inches is easier to control and store. Choose by hand size and drawer space. If your hands are small or your drawer is crowded, the compact pair is the practical choice.

faq.q: Can I cut other foods with them?
faq.a: Yes, the SASACIA listing mentions lettuce and green onions. Cutting paper or crafts can dull the blades. Keep herb scissors for food. Wipe the blades clean after every food use so nothing carries over.

Multi-blade pairs are harder to sharpen at home. Gentle cleaning and avoiding hard materials help the edge last. If a pair dulls, replacement is often easier than sharpening. If a pair dulls or loosens, replacing it is usually simpler than repair.
